metrics.label: Improved sales conversion rates and lowered churn.

sections.title: Context
sections.body: Telefonica / O2, cloud computing services for business customers. I led the user journey work from research through to stakeholder workshops.

sections.title: Problem
sections.body: Sales teams were losing deals they should have won. Support volumes were high. Customers — particularly in SMEs — were struggling to get started. Nobody had mapped the full experience from a customer's perspective, so problems were being solved in isolation by separate teams who had no visibility of each other's pain points. The commercial impact was measurable: conversion and churn were moving in the wrong direction.

sections.title: My role
sections.body: I led the research, journey mapping, and cross-functional workshop facilitation. I personally conducted the customer and stakeholder interviews, produced the journey maps, and ran the co-creation sessions with sales, support, and product teams. Design and implementation of specific fixes were handed to the relevant teams.

sections.title: Approach
sections.body: Research covered customers at different stages — recent sign-ups, active users, churned accounts — and internal stakeholders across sales, support, onboarding, and account management. From this I mapped the full journey across every touchpoint, identifying gaps between what customers needed and what they were experiencing. Several friction points stood out: onboarding assumed technical knowledge many SME buyers didn't have; sales materials didn't address actual customer questions; support was handling queries that better documentation would have prevented. I facilitated cross-functional workshops to align sales and support teams — who rarely had visibility of each other's problems — around the same journey map.

sections.title: Outcome
sections.body:
• Sales conversion rates increased following sales material updates aligned to actual customer questions
  • Churn decreased as onboarding improved and customers reached value faster
  • The cross-functional workshop format became a repeatable model used for subsequent service reviews
